items.headline: Pruneyard owners seek more time on Campbell approvals
items.summary: The October 20 City Council agenda listed an application from the Pruneyard Center Association to amend its Master Use Permit. The amendment would extend the approval phasing deadlines for Phases 3 and 4.

items.headline: Council agenda covers leasing city-owned property at 22100 Stevens Creek Boulevard
items.summary: The City Council's October 20 agenda listed a proposed approach for leasing the city-owned commercial property at 22100 Stevens Creek Boulevard. The item concerns how the city would bring in a tenant for a property it owns along one of Cupertino's main commercial corridors.

items.headline: AT&T seeks to add antennas to two utility poles near Guinda and Homer
items.summary: The October 15 Architectural Review Board agenda listed an AT&T request to add antennas, radio units and seven-foot fiberglass pole extensions to two city-owned wood utility poles in the public right-of-way. The poles are near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue, and the item was filed as exempt from environmental review under the existing-facilities category.

items.headline: Council agenda: El Niño, Anderson Dam and Pure Water updates
items.summary: The October 13 City Council agenda listed a joint update on El Niño preparedness for the 2026-2027 rainy season. It also listed updates on the Anderson Dam Seismic Retrofit and Coyote Creek Flood Protection projects, and on the Pure Water Silicon Valley potable reuse project.

items.headline: Council agenda lists release of documents on offer to buy Cubberley
items.summary: The October 13 City Council agenda included an item on the potential release of documents related to an offer to purchase the Cubberley Community Center property. Cubberley is the city's large community center and school-site campus in south Palo Alto.

items.headline: Peery Park plan amendment would add office, R&D, housing, and move water tower
items.summary: The Planning Commission's October 12 special study session agenda listed a proposed amendment to the Peery Park Specific Plan that would increase office and R&D square footage and residential units, and allow the Libby Water Tower to be relocated. The same session was a scoping meeting to take public comments on the Notice of Preparation for a Supplemental EIR to the 2016 Peery Park plan EIR.
